first-controller.title: Create Your First Controller
first-controller.description: Learn the basics of creating api-ape controllers

steps.title: Understanding Controllers
steps.content: Controllers in api-ape are simple JavaScript files in your `api/` directory. Each exported function becomes an endpoint that clients can call.

steps.title: Create a Controller File
steps.description: Create a new file in your api/ directory

steps.title: Export a Function
steps.description: Export a function from your controller that returns a value

steps.title: Test Your Endpoint
steps.description: Call your endpoint from a client to verify it works

steps.title: Controller Created!
steps.content: Congratulations! You've created your first api-ape controller. Your endpoint is now available at `api.greet.yourFunction()`.

broadcast-master.title: Master Broadcasting
broadcast-master.description: Learn to broadcast messages to all connected clients

steps.title: What is Broadcasting?
steps.content: Broadcasting sends a message to ALL connected clients simultaneously. This is useful for real-time updates like notifications, chat messages, or live data feeds.

steps.title: Broadcast to Others
steps.content: Use `this.broadcastOthers()` to send to all clients EXCEPT the caller. Perfect for chat apps where the sender already knows their own message.

steps.title: Create a Broadcast Endpoint
steps.description: Create a controller that uses this.broadcast() to send a message to all clients
steps.hint: Create a function that calls this.broadcast({...})

steps.title: Test Your Broadcast
steps.description: Open two browser tabs and verify both receive the broadcast
steps.hint: Call your broadcast endpoint from one tab and see the message in both

steps.title: Broadcast Master!
steps.content: You've mastered broadcasting! You can now send real-time updates to all connected clients.

steps.title: What is Pub/Sub?
steps.content: Pub/Sub (Publish/Subscribe) lets you subscribe to specific channels and receive messages published to them. Unlike broadcasting, you only receive messages from channels you're subscribed to.

steps.title: Subscription Syntax
steps.content: Use `api.subscribe.channel.name(callback)` to subscribe. The channel name can be any path - it's automatically created when you subscribe.

steps.title: Create a Subscription
steps.description: Subscribe to a channel in your client code

steps.title: Publish a Message
steps.content: On the server, use `this.publish.channel.name(data)` or `ape.publish.channel.name(data)` to send messages to subscribers.

steps.title: First Subscriber!
steps.content: You've learned pub/sub messaging! Use subscriptions for targeted real-time updates.

basic-auth.title: Implement Basic Authentication
basic-auth.description: Secure your endpoints with Tier 1 authentication

steps.title: Authentication Tiers
steps.content:
api-ape supports 4 authentication tiers:

- **Tier 0 (Guest)**: No authentication
- **Tier 1 (Basic)**: OPAQUE/PAKE or SSO
- **Tier 2 (Elevated)**: Tier 1 + MFA
- **Tier 3 (High Security)**: 2-of-3 Shamir Secret Sharing

steps.title: Set Up Auth Framework
steps.content: Configure the authentication framework with OPAQUE (password-authenticated key exchange) where the server never sees the raw password.

steps.title: Protect an Endpoint
steps.description: Add authentication checking to a controller endpoint

steps.title: Tier 1 Secured!
steps.content: Your endpoints are now protected with basic authentication. Next step: add MFA for Tier 2!

steps.title: What are Lifecycle Hooks?
steps.content: Lifecycle hooks let you run code at key moments: when clients connect, disconnect, send messages, or receive responses.

steps.title: onConnect Hook
steps.content:
The `onConnect` hook fires when a client establishes a WebSocket connection. Use it to:
- Validate connections
- Attach custom data to the socket
- Send welcome messages

steps.title: Implement a Hook
steps.description: Add an onConnect or onDisconnect hook to your server
steps.hint: Add the hook in your ape() configuration

steps.title: Hook Master!
steps.content: You've mastered lifecycle hooks. Use them to control every aspect of client connections.

file-upload.title: Upload Your First File
file-upload.description: Learn binary file transfers with api-ape

steps.title: Binary File Transfers
steps.content: api-ape supports efficient binary file uploads over WebSocket. Files are streamed in chunks, making it memory-efficient for large files.

steps.title: Server-Side Handler
steps.content: On the server, binary data arrives as ArrayBuffer. You can save it to disk or process it.

steps.title: Implement File Upload
steps.description: Create a file upload endpoint and client code

steps.title: File Uploader!
steps.content: You can now handle binary file uploads. Next: try downloading files!

error-handling.title: Handle Errors Gracefully
error-handling.description: Learn to catch and handle API errors properly

steps.title: Why Error Handling Matters
steps.content: API calls can fail for many reasons: network issues, server errors, invalid input, or authentication failures. Proper error handling ensures your app remains responsive and provides helpful feedback to users.

steps.title: Types of Errors
steps.content:
api-ape errors include useful information:

- **message**: Human-readable error description
- **code**: Error code (e.g., 'NOT_FOUND', 'UNAUTHORIZED')
- **status**: HTTP-like status code (404, 401, 500)
- **details**: Additional error context

steps.title: Add Error Handling
steps.description: Wrap an api-ape call in a try/catch block and handle the error appropriately

steps.title: Error Handler!
steps.content: You now know how to handle API errors gracefully. Your users will thank you!

connection-handling.title: Handle Reconnections
connection-handling.description: Learn to handle WebSocket reconnections gracefully

steps.title: Why Reconnection Matters
steps.content: WebSocket connections can drop unexpectedly due to network changes, server restarts, or mobile devices going to sleep. api-ape automatically reconnects, but your app should handle this gracefully.

steps.title: Buffered Calls
steps.content: When disconnected, api-ape buffers your API calls and sends them when reconnected. This makes your code simpler - just call the API and it will work when possible.

steps.title: Handle Reconnection
steps.description: Add a state change handler that shows different UI states based on connection status

steps.title: Connection Pro!
steps.content: You've mastered reconnection handling. Your app now provides a smooth experience even with unstable connections.

connection-states.title: Master Connection States
connection-states.description: Use all WebSocket connection states effectively

steps.title: The 6 Connection States
steps.content:
api-ape tracks 6 distinct connection states:

- **offline**: No network connection (navigator.onLine = false)
- **walled**: Behind a captive portal (hotel/airport WiFi)
- **disconnected**: Has network but not connected to server
- **connecting**: Establishing WebSocket connection
- **connected**: Active connection, ready for API calls
- **closing**: Connection shutting down

steps.title: Special States
steps.content:
Some states require special handling:

- **walled**: User needs to complete captive portal login
- **offline**: Show offline mode UI
- **connecting**: Show reconnecting indicator

steps.title: Handle All States
steps.description: Create a connection status indicator that responds to all connection states
steps.hint: Use a switch statement in onStateChange

steps.title: State Manager!
steps.content: You've mastered all connection states! Your app now handles every network scenario gracefully.

first-publish.title: Publish Your First Message
first-publish.description: Learn to publish messages to channels from the server

steps.title: Publishing vs Broadcasting
steps.content: While broadcasting sends to ALL clients, publishing sends only to clients subscribed to a specific channel. This is more efficient and allows targeted messaging.

steps.title: Publish Syntax
steps.content: Use `this.publish.channel.path(data)` in controllers, or `ape.publish.channel.path(data)` from anywhere (like timers or external events).

steps.title: Create a Publisher
steps.description: Create a controller that publishes messages to a channel

steps.title: Publisher!
steps.content: You can now publish targeted messages to channel subscribers. Perfect for real-time features like live updates, notifications, and chat rooms!

controller-context.title: Master Controller Context
controller-context.description: Use all controller context methods effectively

steps.title: The Controller Context
steps.content: Every controller function receives a rich context via `this`. This includes client info, communication methods, and authentication state.

steps.title: Communication Methods
steps.content:
The context provides several ways to communicate with clients:

- `this.broadcast(msg)` - Send to all clients
- `this.broadcastOthers(msg)` - Send to all except caller
- `this.publish.channel(data)` - Send to channel subscribers
- `this.send(msg)` - Send directly to this client

steps.title: Client Agent Info
steps.content: The `this.agent` object provides detailed browser/device information parsed from the User-Agent header.

steps.title: Use Context Methods
steps.description: Create an endpoint that uses at least 3 different context properties or methods
steps.hint: Combine clientId, agent info, broadcast, etc.

steps.title: Context Expert!
steps.content: You've mastered the controller context! You can now build sophisticated server-side logic with full client awareness.

mfa-setup.title: Enable Multi-Factor Authentication
mfa-setup.description: Add MFA to reach Tier 2 authentication

steps.title: What is MFA?
steps.content:
Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) requires users to prove their identity with multiple factors:

- **Something you know**: Password (Tier 1)
- **Something you have**: Phone/security key (Tier 2)
- **Something you are**: Biometrics (advanced)

api-ape supports WebAuthn (hardware keys, Face ID) and TOTP (authenticator apps).

steps.title: WebAuthn Setup
steps.content: WebAuthn uses hardware security keys or platform authenticators (Touch ID, Face ID, Windows Hello) for strong authentication.

steps.title: TOTP Setup
steps.content: Time-based One-Time Passwords (TOTP) work with authenticator apps like Google Authenticator, Authy, or 1Password.

steps.title: Add MFA Check
steps.description: Create an endpoint that requires Tier 2 authentication

steps.title: MFA Guardian!
steps.content: You've implemented MFA! Your users now have an extra layer of security protecting their accounts.

steps.title: Tier 2 Authentication
steps.content:
Tier 2 authentication combines:

- **Tier 1**: Password authentication (OPAQUE/PAKE)
- **Tier 2**: Multi-factor authentication (WebAuthn or TOTP)

Users must complete both to reach Tier 2. This provides strong security while remaining user-friendly.

steps.title: Elevation Flow
steps.content: Users can be prompted to elevate their authentication for sensitive operations. The elevation is temporary and tied to the session.

steps.title: Implement Tier 2 Flow
steps.description: Create an endpoint that requires Tier 2 and returns elevation info if not met

steps.title: Security Shield!
steps.content: You've implemented complete Tier 2 authentication! Your app now supports secure MFA-protected operations.

tier-3-auth.title: Implement Tier 3 Authentication
tier-3-auth.description: Use Shamir Secret Sharing for highest security

steps.title: Tier 3: Maximum Security
steps.content:
Tier 3 uses **Shamir Secret Sharing** to split cryptographic keys across multiple locations. To authenticate, the user must provide 2-of-3 shares:

- **Device share**: Stored on user's device
- **Server share**: Stored encrypted on your server
- **Recovery share**: Written down or stored in password manager

Even if one share is compromised, the account remains secure.

steps.title: Shamir Secret Sharing Setup
steps.content: When a user enables Tier 3, their key is split into 3 shares. They must keep their recovery share safe - if they lose 2 shares, account recovery becomes complex.

steps.title: Tier 3 Verification
steps.content: To reach Tier 3, the client provides 2 shares. The server combines them with its share to verify authenticity.

steps.title: Protect with Tier 3
steps.description: Create an endpoint that requires Tier 3 authentication for maximum security

steps.title: Fortress!
steps.content: You've implemented Tier 3 authentication with Shamir Secret Sharing! This is enterprise-grade security for your most critical operations.

custom-plugin.title: Create a Custom Plugin
custom-plugin.description: Extend api-ape with your own plugin

steps.title: What are Plugins?
steps.content:
Plugins extend api-ape's functionality. They can:

- Add middleware for all requests
- Inject context methods into controllers
- Add client-side features
- Integrate with external services

steps.title: Adding Context Methods
steps.content: Plugins can add methods to the controller context (`this`). This is useful for shared functionality across endpoints.

steps.title: Registering Plugins
steps.content: Register plugins when initializing api-ape. They're loaded in order, so later plugins can depend on earlier ones.

steps.title: Create Your Plugin
steps.description: Create a plugin that adds at least one context method
steps.hint: Export an object with name and context properties

steps.title: Plugin Master!
steps.content: You've created your first api-ape plugin! Plugins are a powerful way to extend and customize api-ape for your needs.

forest-setup.title: Configure Forest
forest-setup.description: Set up distributed state with Forest database adapters

steps.title: What is Forest?
steps.content:
Forest is api-ape's distributed mesh system. It allows multiple api-ape servers to:

- Share connected client state
- Broadcast across all servers
- Publish/subscribe across the cluster
- Maintain consistent session state

This enables horizontal scaling while keeping real-time features working.

steps.title: Database Adapters
steps.content:
Forest supports multiple database adapters for state synchronization:

- **Redis**: Fast, widely supported, pub/sub built-in
- **PostgreSQL**: LISTEN/NOTIFY for pub/sub
- **MongoDB**: Change streams for sync
- **Custom**: Implement your own adapter

steps.title: Cluster-Wide Broadcasting
steps.content: With Forest configured, all communication methods automatically work across the cluster.

steps.title: Configure Forest
steps.description: Add Forest configuration to your api-ape setup
steps.hint: Add forest: { adapter, config } to ape()

steps.title: Forest Architect!
steps.content: You've configured Forest! Your api-ape servers can now work together as a distributed cluster.

cluster-deployment.title: Deploy a Multi-Server Cluster
cluster-deployment.description: Scale horizontally with multiple api-ape servers

steps.title: Why Multi-Server?
steps.content:
A single server has limits. Multi-server deployment provides:

- **Scalability**: Handle more concurrent connections
- **Reliability**: No single point of failure
- **Geographic distribution**: Lower latency for global users
- **Zero-downtime deployments**: Roll updates gradually

steps.title: Load Balancer Setup
steps.content: WebSocket connections require sticky sessions - once a client connects to a server, they must stay on that server for the duration of the connection.

steps.title: Docker Compose Cluster
steps.content: Use Docker Compose to easily run a local cluster for testing.
steps.codeExample:
# docker-compose.yml
version: '3.8'
services:
  redis:
    image: redis:alpine
    ports: ['6379:6379']

  api-1:
    build: .
    environment:
      - PORT=3001
      - REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379
    depends_on: [redis]

  api-2:
    build: .
    environment:
      - PORT=3002
      - REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379
    depends_on: [redis]

  nginx:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports: ['3000:80']
    volumes:
      - ./nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf
    depends_on: [api-1, api-2]

steps.title: Health Checks
steps.content: Add health check endpoints for load balancers and orchestrators to monitor server health.

steps.title: Create Cluster Config
steps.description: Set up configuration for running multiple api-ape instances
steps.hint: Create docker-compose.yml or add health endpoints

steps.title: Cluster Commander!
steps.content: You've mastered multi-server deployment! Your api-ape cluster can now scale horizontally to handle any load.
